summary: DNACalibLibTest references the Private directory of DNCalibLib module

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: MetaHuman
components.description: Issues for MetaHuman team - FYI MetaHuman has their own Jira space, so this is for connecting UE Jiras to MetaHuman Jiras

content.text: DNACalibLibTest references the Private directory of DNCalibLib

UBT is working towards adding a new setting to check if modules are referencing the private directories of other modules. (-ModuleIncludePrivateWarningLevel=Warning). Eventually this check is to be enabled by default
Additionally our reasons for adding adding this check are:
Prevent hotfix issues created by outside-of-epic-plugins having the ability to reference Private files
Speed up compile times by having a smaller surface area of cross dependencies
Also benefits C++20 header units if/when implemented

I've tried to assign the Component that describes the module including the path first, please change the component if inappropriate. I wasn't completely sure on the component for this Plugin, assigned MetaHuman based on
https://p4-swarm.epicgames.net/changes/24557082
Fixing:

Check that the private include path and the included headers are actually necessary, if not then simply removing the entry in the Module.Build.cs will resolve the warning. There is a slim chance this will be the case

Headers will need to be refactored in the included module to move the required references in the Private/ headers to Public/ or Internal/ headers instead, the private Include Path will then need to be removed from the Module.Build.cs and replaced with PublicIncludePathModuleNames or PrivateIncludePathModuleNames depending on the usage. This is the most likely fix

This will most likely require changes from the code owners of the module being referenced to ensure other modules aren't affected negatively and that APIs aren't exposed publicly when they should be internal only
Internal/ is only available for other engine modules (anything under the Engine/ directory)
Internal/ for all intents should be treated as Public/, any headers in those directories can not be modified in hotfixes
Be careful, there are some private include paths that when replaced with module references could violate rules against including editor or client only modules where they should not be referenced
It's very easy to accidently break other platform compiles & projects like fortnite when changing include paths, run an engine preflight with enough coverage to ensure there are no side effects

summary: GitHub 6560 : Factor blend weights into BlendSpace playrate when using sync markers as Leader

issuetype.description: Pull requests submitted through Unreal Engine Github that are automatically reflected in jira
issuetype.name: GitHub PR

components.name: UE - Anim - Runtime
components.description: Issues related to core animation runtime, blending, anim graph nodes, anim instances, anim sequences

content.text: See
https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine/pull/6560
(shelved in CL 11029621)

Animations of different lengths in a BlendSpace currently do no length adjustment when the Leader, which gives a jarring snap when the highest weighted animation changes. Essentially, having sync markers directly breaks rate adjustments from differing lengths and most interpolation options.

While MoveDelta can't be used like it is for the non-sync'd case, it can be adjusted by a factor of the length difference from the default for the Leader-case. This fixes the problem and also works with the interpolation options. From tests with sync-markers, this looks like it works correctly and gives a substantially better result with different length animations, and re-enables interpolation options.
As I understand Leader/Follower, it should be fine for the Leader to manipulate its play-rate in this way as in this case this instance would be the authority on playback anyway.
Modified Files:
//UE4/Main/Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Animation/BlendSpaceBase.cpp (edit)

The support team will close the pull request when this ticket is marked fixed. Please include a #6560 tag somewhere in the description of any p4 changelists related to this pull request, so that GitHub can cross-reference it.

content.text: Blend Profiles store per bone blend override information in a linear array (ProfileEntries)
Which is then searched linearly at runtime to get the FBlendProfileBoneEntry for each bone that has one.

This linear array is potentially very large - eg if I apply one setting to all of the upper body recursively from the spine, that could include hundreds of entries, and in the worst case, it could have one entry for every bone in the skeleton.
In the worst case this algorithm is O(n^2):
for each bone, look up bone in blend profile array, do blending.
When the task itself could be O
if it were not for the linear array lookup.

summary: Run Construction Script in Sequencer could trigger AnimNotify every frame

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.
issuetype.name: Bug

content.text: When the "Run Construction Script in Sequencer" flag is enabled for an actor and it is bound to a level sequence, the animation sequence's montage instance is recreated every frame during playback.

Such newly initialized animation montage does not have any playback context, but by calling FAnimMontageInstance::SetSequencerMontagePosition(), the instance is set to the expected frame of the playing sequencer. This function also calls another function, SetNextPositionWithEvents(InFromPosition, InToPosition), to try evaluating events between the previous time position and the current time position to trigger anim notifies.

However, instead of evaluating AnimNotifies between the previous frame and the current frame, the instance refers to the previous play position of the instance (which is always 0.0 in this scenario where a montage instance is created every frame) and InToPosition to list events for handling. As a result, this causes the AnimNotifies to be triggered every frame after the Notify frame has passed.
I don't think this is the best fix, but here's a temporary fix for this issue is to modify the following line in Engine\Source\Runtime\Engine\Private\Animation\AnimMontage.cpp around line 2416:

- const float PreviousSubStepPosition = Position;
+ const float PreviousSubStepPosition = ForcedNextFromPosition.IsSet() ? ForcedNextFromPosition.GetValue() : Position;

summary: Montage Editor calls NotifyEnds of AnimNotifyState even when paused

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.
issuetype.name: Bug

content.text: In the Animation Montage Editor, NotifyEnd is unexpectedly called when a time marker is in the middle of an AnimNotifyState and the animation preview gets paused. Because the Animation Montage Editor does not fill AnimInstance->NotifyQueue when it is paused. As a result, any existing AnimNotifyState that was in effect at the last frame is considered finished.

This can be inconsistent behavior. The other editors, such as the Animation Sequence editor, do NOT call NotifyEnd in the same scenario. (The downside is that NotifyTick is always called, even when the animation preview is paused.)

If we let the Animation Montage editor behave the same as the other animation editor, the possible solution is to call HandleEvents() function from FAnimMontageInstance::Advance()  in AnimMontage.cpp even when bPlaying is false.
The customer who reported this issue confirms that it can be fixed by calling HandleEvents() in a case where bPlaying is false.

summary: Placing a section at the end of montage is not properly handled

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.

components.name: UE - Anim - Gameplay
components.description: Issues relating to Locomotion, Contextual Animations, Root Motion, Intertial Blending. Do not use this component for gameplay framework related issues, that is a different team and have their own component; for eg - Gameplay.

content.text: Placing a  section at the very end of a montage with no duration or animation assigned after it is not properly handled.
Normally sections with 0 length are skipped and search continues since they do not pass the check for
UAnimMontage::IsWithinPos()
, ** this is true for all cases except if the montage section is at the end (since the search passes before continuing reaching the last section).
Therefore this causes issues when querying the current section and/or breaks a montage loop determined by linking sections together since the last section is never reached.
Therefore we need to either issue a warning when placing a section at the very end or properly handle that edge case.
